name: webcontent-filter.plugin
title: WebContentFilter:Plugin
description: The declaration to configure a WebContent Filter that uses a plugin.

payloadkeys.title: Visible name
payloadkeys.content: The name of the web content filter that the system displays on the device.

payloadkeys.title: Plugin bundle ID
payloadkeys.content: The bundle ID of the plug-in that provides filtering service. Consult your filtering solution vendor to determine what to specify for this value.

payloadkeys.title: Content filter UUID
payloadkeys.content: A globally unique identifier for this content filter configuration. The content filter processes network traffic for managed apps with the same `ContentFilterUUID` in their app attributes. This key must be present for unsupervised devices and user enrollment.

payloadkeys.title: Server address
payloadkeys.content: The server address, which may be the IP address, hostname, or URL.

payloadkeys.title: Organization
payloadkeys.content: The organization string to pass to the third-party plug-in.

payloadkeys.title: Vendor config
payloadkeys.content: The custom dictionary that the filtering service plug-in needs.

subkeys.content: The custom key/value pairs for the filtering service.

subkeys.title: Credentials asset reference
subkeys.content: The identifier of an asset declaration that contains the credentials (user name and password) to authenticate with the service.

subkeys.title: Identity asset reference
subkeys.content: The identifier of a credential asset declaration that contains the identity that this account requires to authenticate with the service.

subkeys.title: Filter grade
subkeys.content: The system uses this value to derive the relative order of content filters. Filters with a grade of `firewall` see network traffic before filters with a grade of `inspector`. However, the system doesn't define the order of filters within a grade.

subkeys.title: Browser filter details
subkeys.content: Settings that control the browser filter. If not present, the system doesn't use browser filtering.

subkeys.title: Enable browser filter
subkeys.content: If `true`, the system enables filtering WebKit traffic.

subkeys.title: Socket filter details
subkeys.content: Settings that control the socket filter. If not present, the system doesn't use socket filtering.

subkeys.title: Enable socket filter
subkeys.content: If `true`, enables the filtering of socket traffic.

subkeys.title: Data provider composed identifier
subkeys.content:
The data provider identifier. This string identifies the filter data provider when the filter starts running. Required when Enabled is true.

In iOS and visionOS, the identifier is a bundle ID, for example, "com.example.app".

In macOS, the identifier is a composed identifier. The format of the composed identifier is "Bundle-ID {Designated-Requirement}". "Bundle-ID" is the bundle identifier string of the provider. "Designated-Requirement" is the designated requirement string the device uses to match the code signature of the provider. For example, "com.example.app {anchor apple generic}".

subkeys.title: Packet filter details
subkeys.content: Settings that control the packet filter. If not present, the system doesn't use packet filtering.

subkeys.title: Enable packet filter
subkeys.content: If `true`, the system enables filtering network packets.

subkeys.title: Packet provider composed identifier
subkeys.content:
The packet provider identifier. This string identifies the filter data provider when the filter starts running. Required when Enabled is true.

The identifier is a composed identifier. The format of the composed identifier is "Bundle-ID {Designated-Requirement}". "Bundle-ID" is the bundle identifier string of the provider. "Designated-Requirement" is the designated requirement string the device uses to match the code signature of the provider. For example, "com.example.app {anchor apple generic}".

subkeys.title: URL filter details
subkeys.content: Settings that control the URL filter. If not present, the system doesn't use URL filtering.

subkeys.title: Enable URL filter
subkeys.content: If `true`, the system filters URL requests.

subkeys.title: URL filter parameters.
subkeys.content: A dictionary containing URL filter parameters. Required when `Enabled` is `true`.

subkeys.title: Control provider composed identifier
subkeys.content:
The URL filter control provider identifier. This string identifies the filter data provider when the filter starts running. Required when Enabled is true.

In iOS, the identifier is a bundle ID, for example, "com.example.app".

In macOS, the identifier is a composed identifier. The format of the composed identifier is "Bundle-ID {Designated-Requirement}". "Bundle-ID" is the bundle identifier string of the provider. "Designated-Requirement" is the designated requirement string the device uses to match the code signature of the provider. For example, "com.example.app {anchor apple generic}".

subkeys.title: Private information retrieval server settings.
subkeys.content: A dictionary containing Private Information Retrieval server settings.

subkeys.title: Private information retrieval server URL
subkeys.content: The URL containing the domain name of the private information retrieval server.

subkeys.title: Privacy pass issuer URL
subkeys.content: The URL containing the domain name of Privacy Pass Issuer.

subkeys.title: Authentication token asset reference
subkeys.content: The identifier of an asset declaration containing the HTTP bearer token required to authenticate with the service. The bearer token is provided in the `Password` field of the asset data. The system uses this token to attest that it's a valid user when requesting anonymous authentication tokens for PIR exchanges.

subkeys.title: URL filter fail closed
subkeys.content: If `true`, the system blocks URLs if the filter is enabled, but it fails to make any filtering decision; for example, if there's a communication failure with the PIR server. If `false`, the system allows URLs if the filter is enabled, but it fails to make any filtering decision.

subkeys.title: Prefilter fetch frequency
subkeys.content: The time interval in seconds that the system uses to periodically run the `NEURLFilterControlProvider` app extension. The default value is 86400 seconds (1 day). The minimum allowed value is 2700 seconds (45 minutes). The system allows `NEURLFilterControlProvider` implementations to download prefilter Bloom filter data onto the device periodically at the specified interval. Implementations need to allow for a slight difference between the scheduled time and the actual runtime of the task, due to the scheduling mechanism on the system.
